title: The CLI inherits no flag from PHP, and `nvs --help` opens with which build is answering
scope:
which short flags `nvs` declares and where each one comes from; the removal of `nvs -i`;
and the two-line banner that replaces the one-line `about` string. Not in scope: what `nvs info`
reports, which is [0065](0065.md)'s and unchanged; and not the subcommand set, which each command's
own record owns.
dependsOnText: [0065](0065.md), which created `nvs info` and the `-i` alias this record retires.
validatedBy:
`crates/nvs-cli/src/main.rs`'s argument definitions — two short flags in the whole
top-level surface, both generated by clap — and `nvs info`'s own snapshot of the build facts.

summary.headline: The nvs command line drops inherited PHP flags, and --help names the build
summary.body:
Novis copies PHP's semantics, never its command line. The one inherited flag, nvs -i, is gone,
with the derived --info spelling and the global --licenses that hung off it; nvs info is now
spelled one way. The -h and -V flags stay, since they come from the argument parser and Unix
convention, not PHP. And --help now opens with two lines: the project title as the README states
it, then the version, commit and date of the build answering. That date is the commit's, not the
build's, so rebuilds stay identical.
